en: Using a ramp to load heavy boxes reduces the lifting force needed, preventing back injuries.
Using a flagpole pulley changes the direction of your pull, allowing you to safely raise a heavy flag.
Wearing shoes with deep treads increases friction, preventing you from slipping on wet or muddy ground.
Applying powder to sweaty hands reduces friction, preventing painful blisters when playing sports or climbing ropes.
Gravity pulls unsupported objects downward, so keeping heavy items on lower shelves prevents dangerous falling accidents.
Strong neodymium magnets can erase magnetic strips and damage internal components of smartphones and computers.
Water conducts electricity, so you must never touch plugged-in appliances with wet hands to avoid fatal shocks.
Plugging too many high-wattage appliances into one extension cord causes overheating and can start electrical fires.
Ultraviolet light from the sun can damage skin cells, making sunscreen necessary to prevent sunburns and skin cancer.
Listening to headphones at maximum volume for long periods can permanently damage the hair cells in your inner ear.
Metal pot handles get hot through conduction, so using dry oven mitts prevents severe hand burns.
Your body converts chemical energy from nutritious food into mechanical energy, giving you the power to run and play.
